title.en: Music structure mapped into a spatial scene

summary: Map supplied musical events and sections to authored spatial parameters while keeping timing data, audio playback and visual interpretation separate.
objective: Build a seekable scene where measures, phrases and accents drive object arrangement, light or motion through explicit mappings and non-audio alternatives.
example_prompts: Map a supplied verse/chorus/beat JSON timeline onto a sculptural scene with a readable static score view.
negative_signals: Not acoustic simulation, automatic music understanding, emotion inference or proof of synchronization quality.
not_for: No unlabeled waveform-derived semantics, unlicensed media, loudness calibration or mandatory visual style.

entities.name: Musical event track
entities.guidance: Store supplied tempo changes, section/beat IDs and event times as versioned data with provenance; audio is optional and separately licensed.

entities.name: Mapping graph
entities.guidance: Each visual parameter names its source event, transform/range, easing and fallback; multiple events may layer only through declared precedence.

state_contract.model: Model time is seconds from an immutable composition revision. A supplied finite tempo/section/event track maps event IDs to visual targets through explicit functions. Audio playback, when present, uses one audio clock as synchronization authority; visual frames sample that clock and never feed animation drift back into event time. Seek reconstructs active intervals and latched events from data. Missing audio retains captions, section labels and a static event list; changing a mapping creates a new revision and invalidates old checkpoints.
state_contract.authority: Three.js owns the versioned semantic state, model time, history and reset; Blender/glTF assets are named presentation resources only.
actions: Inspect or disable one event-to-visual mapping.

invariants: Every visual change identifies a source event or authored continuous mapping.
Seeking to the same time and revision restores the same semantic visual parameters.
Audio absence cannot remove section/event information needed for the experience.
Presentation gain cannot alter tempo/event timestamps.
motion_guidance: Drive presentation from a seekable model time and derive every visible transform from current state; pause and scrub never advance hidden semantic state.
Provide a static sequence/list and reduced-motion mode that preserves text, order, choices and status.
creative_affordances: Choose typography, assets, palette, staging and metaphor per the supplied brief and licensed material; no house style is mandatory.
Blender owns expressive geometry, rigs, sets and cue anchors; Three.js owns time, branch/state, captions, interruption and checkpoints.
known_limits: The scene interprets supplied annotations; it does not discover musical form, measure acoustic response or infer audience emotion.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, audio playback, visitor study, show-control link, browser or renderer was run.

claims.statement: The Web Audio API exposes AudioContext currentTime as its time coordinate and schedules source starts and AudioParam changes against that audio timeline.
claims.scope: Web Audio 1.1 browser audio scheduling; availability and output latency remain implementation/runtime concerns.

source_refs.locator: BaseAudioContext currentTime; AudioScheduledSourceNode start; AudioParam automation methods

object_craft.structure: Build stable section islands, beat markers and reusable performer/prop forms keyed by IDs; preserve a legible timeline outside the scene.
object_craft.material: Use shape and labels with color; reactive brightness is a mapped value, not measured sound pressure.

physical_contract.scope: Spatial layout and motion communicate authored media/state; geometry and collisions have no physical authority.
physical_contract.timestep: Evaluate from seekable authored time or discrete event state; no physics integration.
checks: presentation controls leave semantic data unchanged
